name: @561-group/durante
description: durante — a QUAKE-like first-person shooter on @561-group/abrash (software 3D over the daleske pixel terminal). You walk a level, strafe, and shoot a demon. The paraconsistent TWIST rides the substrate three ways. (1) THE ARENA IS A MERGE OF TRACES: the level is not authored once — it SETTLES from the federated union of every player's trace, so a deathmatch arena is the fold of the peers who built it, and where two traces DISAGREE about a wall the substrate holds it ⊤ — a CONTESTED wall that SHIVERS, and a PHASE GATE you can walk through (passContested) precisely because nobody agrees it is solid. (2) A WEAPON'S EFFECT IS EVIDENCE YOU FOLD: a shot does not subtract a hit-point — it APPENDS deny(demon,'alive') to the trace, negative evidence on the demon's vitality. The demon's life is the FOLD of that evidence; the LAW is linear, so every wound is a witness kept, never overwritten. (3) THE ENEMY IS HELD ⊤: between your first wound and the kill, the demon is alive-AND-dead — affirmed alive by its spawn, denied alive by your shots — a held contradiction ⊤, the demon you cannot trust, rendered with a CONTESTED tint, until enough deny-evidence SETTLES it to f (dead) and it falls. ⊤ is not a debug dump here, it is the designed mechanic: the monster that is both until you settle it. THE LAW: ⊤ held, append-only trace, evidence linear. Named for the durante lineage of the id-software fast shooter. Built on @561-group/abrash (+ @561-group/computer); games ride the engine.
